subject: Multinomial data analyses with different category effect

messages.author: 341f1623f3e25733
messages.subject: Multinomial data analyses with different category effect
parts:
Dear INLA group
I have multinomial data and I would like to analyze them with INLA but unfortunately, I can't use http://www.r-inla.org/faq ( FAQ example) because I have rw1 model for every category with different parameter and need to use separate f()
for every one of the category. I have three categories. I still use Multinomial-Poisson transformation. I have used models with more than one type of likelihood. The results of INLA are not close to simulation and I guess the problem is my prior distribution but I can't detect the best one.

code here:

#Producing the effect of time
## first category
t=runif(n,-1,1)
ft1=sin(2*pi*(2*t-1))
##second category
ft2=sin(pi*(2*t-1))
##
epsilon<-rnorm(n)
###linear predictor
eta1<-as.vector(ft1 + epsilon)
eta2<-as.vector(ft2 + epsilon)
eta3<-as.vector(rep(0,n)) # to detect reference category
eta<-cbind(eta1,eta2,eta3)
eta<-as.matrix(eta)
###
pp = matrix(rep(NA,n*m), nc=3)
y<-c()
for(i in 1:n){
p=exp(eta[i,])
prob = p/sum(p)
pp[i,]=prob
yy = rmultinom(1, size =5, prob= prob)
y<-c(y,yy)
}

N=3*n

YY = matrix(NA, N, 3)
YY[1:n, 1]=y1 # first category
YY[1:n + n, 2]=y2 # second category
YY[1:n + 2*n,3]=y3 # third  category

i<-rep(1:n,3)

j1<-rep(NA,N)
j1[1:n]=1:n

j2<-rep(NA,N)
j2[1:n +n]<-1:n +n

j3<-rep(NA,N)
j3[1:n + 2*n]<-1:n + 2*n
i1<-i
 
Data<-data.frame(YY, j1,j2,j3,i,i1)

link = rep(NA, N) 
link[which(is.na(YY[1:n]))] = 1
link[n + which(is.na(YY[1:n + n]))] = 2
link[2*n + which(is.na(YY[1:n + n]))] = 3

formula<- YY~f(j1,model="rw1",hyper = list(prec =
list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.5))))+
f(j2,model="rw1",hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.5))))+
f(j3,model="rw1",hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.5))))+
f(i,model="iid",hyper =list(prec =list(initial=log(0.0001),fixed=TRUE)))+
f(i1,model="iid",hyper =list(prec =list(initial=log(0.0001),fixed=TRUE)))

result = inla(formula,
        family = c("poisson", "poisson", "poisson"),
        data=Data,
        control.predictor = list(link = link))
Could you please help me to solve this problem?

Thanks in advance for helping.

Regards

Leyla
